sourcedFrom: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 (02/2011 (printed as the document code G0232000 - 02/2011; no separate © line))
cleanIntro: Benelli's own strip for the Montefeltro, in Benelli's order. This is an INERTIA gun — no gas piston, no ports, no cylinder to decarbon. The spring inside the bolt that the manual calls the recoil spring is the whole operating system, and it comes out at step 12. Fourteen steps take it to bare parts and Benelli then states the strip is finished. Note the terminology in this book: the part the M2 manual calls the bolt handle is called the COCKING LEVER here, and it comes off with a deliberate tug.

steps.title: Check this book is for your gun — it speaks for a family, and one of them is USA-market only
steps.action: Compare your gun against the list this manual prints on its cover: Montefeltro, Duca di Montefeltro, Comfort, Beccaccia, Centro and Ultralight, with the Ultralight marked as the USA-market variant.
steps.prose: The catalog row says only "Montefeltro" and Benelli sells the name across a family. Everything on this cover shares the one inertia action and one strip, which is why they share one book — but check yours is on the list before you follow it, rather than after.
steps.quote:
Montefeltro Comfort

Duca di Montefeltro Beccaccia

Centro *Ultralight

* USA market
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Cover — model list

steps.title: Safety catch on — the red ring must disappear
steps.action: Press the safety button on the trigger guard until the red ring is no longer visible.
steps.prose: Benelli defines the safe state by what you cannot see rather than by which way the button points. It is a one-second visual check and it comes before the action is worked.
steps.quote: Press the safety button on the trigger guard until its red ring, indicating firing position, is no longer visible (figs. 16-17).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Gun safety catch — p.54

steps.title: Chambered round out, then the bolt eased closed
steps.action: With the safety engaged and the muzzle safe, open the bolt — the chambered cartridge is extracted and ejected. Then close the bolt by gently releasing the cocking lever.
steps.prose: Gently is the instruction. On an inertia gun the bolt slamming home is exactly what recoil is supposed to make it do; doing it by hand on the bench with the barrel about to come off is not the same thing.
steps.quote:
1) Open the bolt: the cartridge in the chamber will be extracted and ejected (fig. 24).
2) Close the bolt: gently releasing the cocking lever (fig. 25).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Unloading, steps 1-2, p.64

steps.title: Prove it empty once more — chamber, carrier AND magazine
steps.action: Before starting any part of the strip, make sure the chamber, the carrier and the magazine are all unloaded.
steps.prose: Benelli reprints this at the head of the stripping section and names three places, not one. Step 1 of the teardown unscrews the fore-end cap off the magazine tube, so a loaded tube is not something to find out about there.
steps.quote: Before starting any operation on your shotgun, make sure that the chamber, carrier and the magazine are unloaded! (Carefully read the instructions on gun loading and unloading).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Shotgun stripping (for cleaning and maintenance) — p.82

steps.title: Fore-end cap off, fore-end forward along the magazine tube
steps.action: Unscrew the fore-end cap and slide the fore-end forward off along the magazine tube.
steps.prose: On this gun the fore-end comes off before the barrel and by itself — unlike the M2, where the barrel and fore-end travel forward together as one unit. Slide it along the tube rather than lifting it away.
steps.quote: Unscrew the fore-end cap and remove the fore-end making it slide forward along the magazine tube (figs. 3-4-5).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 1, p.82

steps.title: Bolt opened and locked back — via the cartridge drop lever if it will not hold
steps.action: Hold the gun in one hand and open the bolt with the other. If the bolt will not stay open, move the cartridge drop lever as arrowed and repeat.
steps.prose: The bolt has to be held open for the barrel to come out. Whether it holds depends on the state of the cut-off feed system, which is what the cartridge drop lever resets — it is not a mysterious extra step.
steps.quote: Take the gun in one hand and with the other open the bolt (fig. 29); should the bolt fail to engage, move the cartridge drop lever as arrowed and repeat the operation (fig. 30).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 2, p.84

steps.title: Stock on the hip, barrel pulled forward out of the receiver
steps.action: Rest the stock on your hip, grip the barrel where it has moved forward clear of the magazine tube, and pull it forward to draw the whole barrel-breech unit out of the receiver.
steps.prose: The stock on the hip is there to give you a straight pull along the axis — the barrel extension is a close fit in the receiver and levering it out at an angle marks both. This is also the moment to look at the locking recesses in the barrel extension while they are in the light.
steps.quote: Pull the barrel forward to remove the whole barrel-breech unit from the receiver (fig. 31).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 4, p.84

steps.title: Bolt eased forward under control, using the carrier button
steps.action: Take a firm hold of the cocking lever and press the carrier button at the same time, letting the bolt run slowly forward until it stops.
steps.prose: Two hands, two jobs. The bolt is coming off its catch under spring pressure and you are lowering it, not dropping it — with the barrel already out, a released bolt hammers into a bare receiver.
steps.quote: Take a firm hold of the cocking lever and simultaneously press the carrier button, thus allowing the bolt to move slowly forward until it stops (figs. 32 and 33).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 5, p.86

steps.title: Cocking lever off with a firm tug
steps.action: Pull the cocking lever straight off with a single firm tug.
steps.prose: This is the step that stops people. The lever is a press fit held by a detent, not a screwed or pinned part, and Benelli's own word is "tug". A hesitant pull will not shift it and will persuade you something is still locked. Pull in line with the lever, not levered up or down.
steps.quote: Pull the cocking lever off with a firm tug (fig. 34).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 6, p.86

steps.title: Bolt assembly slid out of the receiver
steps.action: Pull the bolt assembly out of the receiver, sliding it forward along its guides.
steps.prose: With the lever gone the assembly leaves out the front along its own rails, as one unit — locking head, firing pin and recoil spring still inside. The next steps take that unit apart on the bench.
steps.quote: Pull the bolt assembly out of the receiver, sliding it along its guides (fig. 35).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 7, p.86

steps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out, holding the pin and its spring
steps.action: Remove the firing pin retaining pin from the bolt assembly while holding the firing pin and firing pin spring in place, then remove the firing pin and its spring from the bolt.
steps.prose: Hold before you pull. The firing pin sits on a compressed spring and the retaining pin is the only thing containing it.
steps.quote: Remove the firing pin retaining pin from the bolt assembly, while holding the firing pin and firing pin spring in place (fig. 36).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 8, p.88

steps.title: Locking head rotating pin out, then the locking head off
steps.action: Remove the locking head rotating pin from its seat, then take the bolt locking head off the bolt.
steps.prose: The rotating locking head is what holds the pressure — its lugs turn into the barrel extension you just had in your hand. It comes off only after its pin does; there is no other retention. Look at the lugs and the head's channel while they are apart.
steps.quote: Remove the locking head rotating pin from its seat (fig. 38).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 10, p.88

steps.title: Recoil spring out of its seat in the bolt — the operating system
steps.action: Remove the recoil spring from its seat in the bolt.
steps.prose: This spring inside the bolt IS the Montefeltro's operating system. Under recoil the receiver moves and the bolt body lags, compressing it; it then throws the bolt back to cycle the gun. There are no gas ports on this shotgun, so the state of this spring and its seat is what cleaning is actually for. It goes back in the same seat and nothing else in the gun resembles it.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring from its seat in the bolt (fig. 40).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 12, p.90

steps.title: Trigger group out: pin pushed through, then the group forward
steps.action: Push the trigger guard pin out of the stock-receiver unit from either side, using the point of the firing pin you already removed or any punch. Then press the carrier button and draw the trigger guard assembly out toward the front.
steps.prose: Benelli nominates the firing pin as the tool — it is already in your hand and it is the right diameter. The carrier button must be pressed or the group will not clear; do not lever it out against a held carrier.
steps.quote: Extract the trigger guard pin from the stock-receiver unit, thrusting it from right or left with the point of the same firing pin or punch (fig. 41).
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, step 13, p.90

steps.title: Strip complete — Benelli says so in as many words
steps.action: You have the barrel-breech unit, the fore-end and its cap, the bolt broken down into body, locking head and rotating pin, firing pin and spring with its retaining pin, and the recoil spring, plus the trigger guard assembly with its pin, and the stock-receiver.
steps.prose: There is no deeper published procedure in this book. The trigger group comes out and goes back as an assembly and is not taken apart at this level.
steps.quote: The shotgun is now completely stripped. All the parts that require routine maintenance and cleaning are disassembled.
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Stripping procedure, after step 14, p.90

steps.title: Barrel bore after use
steps.action: Clean the bore normally after every use.
steps.prose: Benelli's whole maintenance position for these guns is four short items and this is the first. An inertia gun has no gas system to service, so the barrel and the two residue traps below are the entire routine.
steps.quote: 1) normal cleaning of the barrel after use;
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Maintenance, item 1, p.78

steps.title: Bolt assembly and trigger group: the two places residue collects
steps.action: Dismantle, clean and lubricate the bolt assembly periodically. Give the firing mechanism — hammer, trigger and the rest of the group — the same periodic cleaning or lubrication.
steps.prose: These are the two places Benelli names for powder residue and foreign matter. On the bolt that means the locking head channel, the firing pin bore and the recoil spring seat you opened at step 12 — the surfaces the system needs free to move.
steps.quote: 3) the bolt assembly may also become clogged with the same residuals over mentioned and therefore must be periodically dismantled, cleaned and lubricated;
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Maintenance, item 3, p.78

steps.title: Oil what the weather can reach
steps.action: Lightly oil the parts exposed to the atmosphere to keep the gun in good order.
steps.prose: This is the anti-corrosion pass, not the lubrication pass — a wiped film on external steel, not oil poured into the action. Flooding the trigger group in the name of protection undoes the previous step.
steps.quote: 4) to keep the gun in good order, oiling of the parts subject to atmospheric corrosion is recommended.
steps.cite: Montefeltro / Duca di Montefeltro / Comfort / Beccaccia / Centro / Ultralight — Uso • Manutenzione | Use • Maintenance — G0232000 - 02/2011 — Maintenance, item 4, p.78

deepAbsentReason: This book publishes ONE teardown, headed "Shotgun stripping (for cleaning and maintenance)", and closes it with "The shotgun is now completely stripped". It already reaches the rotating locking head, the firing pin, the recoil spring inside the bolt and the trigger group. There is no further published user-level disassembly for the Montefeltro to promote into a deep clean.

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Normal cleaning of the bore after use.
Barrel extension locking recesses while the barrel is out — these are the surfaces the rotating head locks into.

cleaning.name: Bolt assembly
tasks: Locking head, its channel in the bolt body, and the rotating pin seat.
Firing pin, firing pin spring and the firing pin bore.
Recoil spring and its seat in the bolt — the operating system of the gun.

cleaning.name: Trigger group
tasks: Hammer, trigger and the rest of the firing mechanism cleaned of powder residue and foreign matter by periodic cleaning or lubrication.
Cleaned as an assembly; not taken apart at this level.

cleaning.name: External surfaces
tasks: Light oil on the parts subject to atmospheric corrosion.

reassembly: Trigger guard assembly back into the receiver with the hammer cocked, pressing the carrier button, then seated home.
Trigger guard pin pushed back through the stock-receiver.
Recoil spring into its seat in the bolt.
Locking head onto the bolt, then the locking head rotating pin into its seat.
Firing pin and firing pin spring into the bolt, held while the firing pin retaining pin goes back in.
Bolt assembly slid into the receiver along its guides; cocking lever pressed firmly home.
Barrel-breech unit into the receiver, pulled square along the magazine tube.
Fore-end slid back along the magazine tube and the fore-end cap screwed down.
fncheck: With the gun proven empty and the muzzle safe: press the safety button until the red ring disappears and confirm it does. Work the cocking lever to confirm the bolt runs and locks back, and that it does not come off in your hand — a cocking lever that was not pressed fully home will. Confirm the trigger guard sits flush in the receiver, and that the fore-end cap is fully screwed down onto the magazine tube.
